```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)   # readr, dplyr, ggplot2 ...
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

impurities <- c("dimer_ppm", "aldehyde_ppm", "chloride_ppm", "ester_ppm", "isomer_ppm")
reference_raw <- read_csv("data-raw/shipment/reference_samples.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
questioned <- read_csv("data-raw/shipment/questioned_samples.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

  pivot_longer(all_of(impurities), names_to = "impurity", values_to = "ppm") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = source, y = ppm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +

## 2. Checking the reference set

<!-- The results were copied by hand from the lab notebooks. Which values can't be right?
     Which samples don't look like their own source? Decide what to do with each one,
     record it in the cleaning log at the end, and then rerun everything below. -->

```{r}
#| label: clean
reference <- reference_raw
# Your decisions, for example:
# reference <- reference |> mutate(ester_ppm = if_else(sample_id == "...", ..., ester_ppm))   # reason: ...
# reference <- reference |> filter(sample_id != "...")                                       # reason: ...
reference <- reference |>
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("Our plant", "Competitor X", "Competitor Y")))
```

```{r}
#| label: distances
# Each sample's squared Mahalanobis distance from the mean of its own source,
# computed without the sample itself (Lesson 2).
loo_distance <- function(i, data) {
  others <- data |> filter(source == data$source[i], sample_id != data$sample_id[i])
  X <- as.matrix(others[, impurities])
  mahalanobis(unlist(data[i, impurities]), colMeans(X), cov(X))
}
reference |>
  mutate(d2 = map_dbl(seq_len(n()), loo_distance, data = reference),
         p_value = pchisq(d2, df = 5, lower.tail = FALSE)) |>
  arrange(desc(d2)) |>
  select(sample_id, source, d2, p_value) |>
  head(8)
```

```{r}
#| label: cv-check
# Reference samples that a cross-validated LDA assigns to a different source (Lesson 13).
cv_check <- MASS::lda(source ~ dimer_ppm + aldehyde_ppm + chloride_ppm + ester_ppm + isomer_ppm,
                      data = reference, CV = TRUE)
reference |>
  mutate(predicted = cv_check$class,
         posterior_predicted = apply(cv_check$posterior, 1, max)) |>
  filter(predicted != source) |>
  select(sample_id, source, predicted, posterior_predicted)
```

## 3. Comparing the fingerprints

<!-- Do the three products differ? Check the assumptions, then find out which impurities
     tell our product apart from each competitor's. -->

```{r}
#| label: manova
fit <- manova(cbind(dimer_ppm, aldehyde_ppm, chloride_ppm, ester_ppm, isomer_ppm) ~ source, data = reference)
summary(fit)
summary.aov(fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: assumptions
#| eval: false
heplots::boxM(reference[, impurities], reference$source)
# Residual normality: a Q-Q plot of each column of resid(fit) (Lesson 3).
```

```{r}
#| label: contrasts
#| eval: false
# Ours against X, and ours against Y (Lesson 7). The levels are in the order
# Our plant, Competitor X, Competitor Y.
X <- as.matrix(reference[, impurities])
levs <- levels(reference$source)
means <- t(sapply(levs, function(s) colMeans(X[reference$source == s, , drop = FALSE])))
n_i <- as.numeric(table(reference$source))
E <- summary(fit)$SS$Residuals
Sp <- E / (nrow(X) - length(levs))
cc <- c(1, -1, 0)                       # ours minus X
psi <- colSums(cc * means)
# T² test of the contrast, and Bonferroni intervals for the five impurities: ...
```

## 4. A classification rule

<!-- Fit the LDA, interpret its discriminants, and estimate its error rate honestly.
     Compare QDA. Which rule would you defend, and why? -->

```{r}
#| label: lda
#| eval: false
rule <- MASS::lda(source ~ dimer_ppm + aldehyde_ppm + chloride_ppm + ester_ppm + isomer_ppm, data = reference)
rule
round(cor(X, predict(rule)$x), 2)   # structure correlations

cv <- MASS::lda(source ~ ..., data = reference, CV = TRUE)
table(true = reference$source, predicted = cv$class)
mean(cv$class != reference$source)
```

## 5. The questioned samples

<!-- For each sample: the most likely source, and the posterior probabilities.
     Q6 has no chloride result: use a rule built without chloride, and check its error rate. -->

```{r}
#| label: classify
#| eval: false
complete <- questioned |> filter(!is.na(chloride_ppm))
pred <- predict(rule, newdata = complete)
tibble(sample_id = complete$sample_id, source = pred$class) |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(round(pred$posterior, 3)))

rule_no_chloride <- MASS::lda(source ~ ..., data = reference)
# Its cross-validated error rate: ...
# Its verdict for Q6: ...
```
